Customization discovery (agents, skills, instructions and workspace MCP configuration) is per chat. A chat anchors to its own effective working directories: its first, plus its others when multi-root is enabled. It never anchors to the session's other folders, so a peer working in a second folder gets that folder's customizations. A fork anchors to its own folder, and a worktree-isolated chat to its worktree. The chats of a session that share an anchor set share one refcounted `CustomizationAnchor` in the session's `SessionPluginController`, so discovery never runs twice for the same set; it is released with the last chat using it, and on session finalize. The session's `ActiveClient` keeps the client tool set and client-synced plugins, so client updates still reach every chat. A chat's snapshot is its anchor set's discoveries plus the session's client contributions. Agent pickers list the session's published (default chat's) agents. So when a chat's selected custom agent isn't discovered by its own anchor set, that one agent is taken from the published anchor set. Its instructions and skills stay its own folder's. `SessionState.customizations` remains the default chat's view, and the published anchor follows the default chat, including after a chat-only move. `copilot.sharedCustomizationDirectories` is still written for older builds but is not read. MCP runtime state is still published to the session by every live chat (last writer wins), so a peer's folder-only MCP servers also appear in the session list.

+Copilot's customization restart comparison uses semantic URI equality for discovered agents and additional-root instructions, retaining ordered, full metadata comparison without comparing the URI's mutable path/serialization caches. SDK launch reads populate those caches; freshly mapped snapshots need not have them. A customization mismatch logs only its first changed component and applied/current counts, distinguishing parsed plugins, discovered agents, additional-root instructions, and evicted relocated roots without their contents.

Steering received during turn preparation or configuration refresh is buffered for the addressed chat. A dispatched turn confirmed running by root SDK events accepts and flushes steering immediately, even if its admission RPC has not returned; successful admission also flushes it. Preparation or send failure retains buffered steering for a successful retry, rather than dispatching against an unready runtime. Pending updates replace or remove buffered steering; abort clears it and emits `steering_consumed` to clear the pending UI. The live SDK-session wrapper takes ownership synchronously before MCP reconciliation, so abort and disposal can clear steering throughout delivery. Chat disposal and host shutdown discard buffered delivery, and pending-message updates are ignored once host shutdown starts.

AHP stores steering and queued messages together in `queuedMessages`, distinguished by `PendingMessage.kind`. Steering entries use `IAgent.sendSteeringMessage` individually, bypassing Copilot's replaceable legacy-slot buffer. The host retries deferred handoff on provider progress and correlates consumption by message ID. A handoff promise that resolves false returns the message unsent because its turn ended first; the host then steers the active turn with it or, once the chat is idle, runs it as the next turn ahead of queued messages. Steering the provider still holds keeps queued work waiting; when a held handoff resolves true while the chat is idle and steering is still pending, for example because sending it failed, the host drains again. Cancellation clears every pending steering entry, including prompts handed off but not yet consumed by the SDK, without draining queued follow-ups. A client may remove handed-off steering during a turn only when the provider implements `IAgent.withdrawSteeringMessage`; Copilot then withdraws it from the SDK with `rpc.queue.withdrawMessage`, or keeps it as its own turn if the model already received it.

A dispose of a session waits for a `createSession` of the same session that was requested before it (`AgentService.disposeSession` and `disposeSessionIf`), so it runs after the provider has registered the draft's provisional chat and disposes it. Creation does not offer such a draft to the prewarmer; otherwise its launch would only be discarded by the expiry below. Creation must never dispose its own session through these entry points (it rolls back the provider chat directly), or it would wait on itself.

-A warm launch is the launch the first send would run, started early and kept on the draft's reservation (`IProvisionalSession.earlyLaunch` in `CopilotAgent`). Its session is registered live, so MCP status and sign-in requests reach it, but it is never persisted, listed or announced until the first send completes it exactly as a cold materialization would. Nothing is applied to it live: when anything fixed at launch has changed by the first send, that send discards it and launches cold. That covers the working directory (always the case for a worktree send), the model or custom agent selection, client tools, plugin or MCP definitions, and the chat's owner. Turn telemetry reports whether the send used it (`usedPrewarmedSession`) or why it discarded it (`prewarmedSessionDiscardReason`). It is also discarded when the chat is disposed, or after 5 unsent minutes. A runtime torn down underneath it (a client restart, closed-connection recovery or idle release) is forgotten while the reservation stays, and its leftover SDK state is deleted before the next launch. An unsent warm launch is never resumed, because the SDK has saved nothing to resume. A worktree draft never warms: its customization enablement stays pending until the worktree is created on the first send. While the setting is on, the Agents window therefore keeps the isolation choice local until Send: it creates every draft in the picked folder, even when the user picked or inherited a worktree, and its first request sends the picked isolation (and base branch) with the rest of the draft's config as a `SessionConfigChanged`, which marks a worktree pending while the session is still creating. That folder draft warms; a worktree send discards the warm launch and starts cold in the new worktree, and a folder send claims it.

Both windows create their draft with the model selected in the chat input (`AgentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService` in the editor window), because the first send selects its model before it runs and discards a launch made with another one (`modelChanged`). In the editor window, a draft whose chat model was disposed is retired, so chat input chips that still show it while the widget switches to the next chat cannot recreate a backend for it.

+Copilot reserves the names of host tools registered for the current launch before registering client tools with the SDK. A host tool omitted from that session does not hide a same-name client tool. Among clients contributing the same name to a chat, its message sender takes precedence, followed by client insertion order. The launcher resolves SDK tools together with a data-only initialization payload (`toolSearch`, `excludedTools`, `systemMessage`, and `customAgents`), then spreads that exact payload into create/resume. At queued configuration boundaries, the session generically compares the applied initialization data with the same resolver's desired data. A mismatch takes the existing relaunch path; otherwise awaited `session.setTools` replaces the complete client-supplied SDK tool set, retaining shell, server, extension, Computer Use, and MCP routing tools. Parsed custom agents and prompt overrides are retained from launch; tool references are remapped without rereading files, and derived set-like tool lists are canonicalized so reordered contributions do not cause needless relaunches. All tool-only changes, including removals and renames, apply at that boundary even during active turns or subagents; the host does not wait for idle or alter the SDK's handling of in-flight tool calls. Applied definitions and routing change only after success; failures propagate and leave the old snapshot available for retry. Already-running tool handlers finish on their original handlers and retain their stamped contributors; subsequent calls use the accepted replacement. Plugin, MCP, directory, model-runtime, and owner changes retain their existing relaunch paths. Calls are routed only to clients whose live definition matches the applied snapshot; an identical reconnect can take over, but a newly connected or updated client cannot execute an incompatible contract before its definition is accepted by the SDK.
